clue.text: Civilised European embracing modern form of technology

indicators.note: embracing means the word for a European wraps round the other piece

parts.note: a Pole is a European from Poland
IT is information technology

explanation.surface: A cultured European takes up the latest technology.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone civilised has good manners, so is courteous and well-mannered.

clue.text: Like a table needed by chemist — I will contribute to it

definitions.text: Like a table needed by chemist — I will contribute to it

parts.words: Like a table needed by chemist — I will contribute to it
parts.note: the chemist's table of elements is the ... one, and the letter I (iodine) is one of its entries, as well as a letter in the word itself

explanation.surface: A chemist needs a particular table and the speaker offers to help with it.
explanation.walkthrough: I is the chemical symbol for iodine, so 'I' does contribute to the chemist's table of the elements.
explanation.definitionFit: The table of chemical elements arranged by atomic number is called the periodic table.

clue.text: Scottish location has women wearing garlands

indicators.note: wearing puts the women's letter inside the garlands, as if dressed in them

parts.note: leis are Hawaiian flower garlands

explanation.surface: A Scottish spot where the women go about in flower garlands.
explanation.walkthrough: Lewis is the northern part of the island of Lewis and Harris in Scotland's Outer Hebrides.
explanation.definitionFit: Lewis is an island area of the Outer Hebrides, a place in Scotland.

clue.text: One attempting to keep two maidens more tidy

indicators.note: to keep means the first piece holds the second within it

parts.note: a trier is one who attempts things
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over, so two of them give a double M

explanation.surface: Someone tries to retain two young women who are neater.
explanation.definitionFit: Trim means neat, so its comparative describes something neater.

clue.text: Critical point when Catholic is bowled over by goddess

indicators.note: bowled over means knocked over, so the Catholic abbreviation is turned round

parts.note: RC is short for Roman Catholic
Isis is the Egyptian goddess

explanation.surface: A cricketing Catholic is dismissed by a goddess at the key moment.
explanation.definitionFit: A turning point of great danger or decision is a critical point.

clue.text: Show convincing evidence once more for rebuke

explanation.surface: Proving a point a second time as a way of telling someone off.
explanation.definitionFit: To reprimand someone is to scold them, and re-proving is demonstrating again.

clue.text: Scottish storyteller in street service finishing prematurely

indicators.note: finishing prematurely means the word loses its last letter

parts.note: evensong is the evening church service

explanation.surface: A Scottish author caught in a road while a church service ends early.
explanation.walkthrough: Robert Louis Stevenson wrote Treasure Island and Kidnapped.
explanation.definitionFit: Robert Louis Stevenson was a celebrated Scottish novelist and teller of tales.

clue.text: Shelter in piggery — is weather like this outside?

indicators.note: in places the word for shelter inside the word for a pig's home

parts.note: a sty is a pigsty
lee means shelter, as in the lee of a wall

explanation.surface: Someone sheltering in a pigsty asks what the weather is doing.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather of mixed rain and snow is described with this adjective.

clue.text: Something attractive has Heather speaking slowly

parts.note: a draw is an attraction that pulls in crowds
ling is a name for common heather

explanation.surface: A woman called Heather has a certain allure as she talks.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heather' looks like a woman's name; here it is the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: A drawl is a lazy, slow way of talking, so its participle fits.

clue.text: Various Tobago girls — one 'talks rubbish'

indicators.note: various suggests the letters are taken in a varied order

explanation.surface: Assorted Caribbean girls, one of whom speaks nonsense.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Various' rearranges TOBAGO GIRLS. The definition plays on '-ologist': one who discourses on a subject, here garbage.
explanation.definitionFit: A student of waste and refuse is jokingly an expert who discusses rubbish.

clue.text: Viewer sees lord outside gym

indicators.note: outside means the lord's word goes round the gym's letters

parts.note: a peer is a lord
PE is physical education, gym class

explanation.surface: A spectator spots a nobleman standing outside the gym.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who peeps or looks at something is an onlooker.

clue.text: See ship dropping

parts.note: lo is an old word meaning look or see
SS is steamship

explanation.surface: Watch the vessel going down.
explanation.definitionFit: A drop in value or numbers is a decline or loss.

clue.text: Sailor outside port with fishing item is entertaining little figure

indicators.note: outside means the sailor's word wraps round the rest

parts.note: a mate is a ship's officer
Rio de Janeiro is a port
a net is used for fishing

explanation.surface: A seaman stands outside a harbour with his net, an amusing little character.
explanation.definitionFit: A puppet worked by strings is a small figure used to entertain.

clue.text: Female dancer gets word of understanding when awful snigger goes round

indicators.note: goes round means the scrambled letters surround the other word
awful suggests a mangled form of the word snigger

parts.note: roger is radio talk for message received and understood

explanation.surface: A dancer hears a radio acknowledgement amid a nasty snigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Female dancer' sounds like any ballerina, but a famous name is wanted; 'word of understanding' is radio jargon for message received.
explanation.definitionFit: Ginger Rogers was the Hollywood dancer famous for partnering Fred Astaire.

clue.text: Restless types chat about expert not in favour

indicators.note: about means the chat word goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to gas is to chatter idly
a dab, as in dab hand, is an expert
out means out of fashion

explanation.surface: Fidgety people gossip about a specialist who has fallen from grace.
explanation.definitionFit: People who flit restlessly from place to place in search of fun are gadabouts.

clue.text: Crazy act — one's called to interrupt it

indicators.note: to interrupt means the second piece breaks into the first

parts.note: a deed is an act
one has called, that is one rang on the phone

explanation.surface: A mad performance, interrupted by someone's phone call.
explanation.definitionFit: Mad and insane are synonyms of crazy.

clue.text: Party with any number under canvas makes one unhappy

parts.note: a disco is a dance party
N stands for an unspecified number in maths
tented means sheltered by canvas

explanation.surface: A dance party for any number of people in a tent makes someone miserable.
explanation.definitionFit: Dissatisfied and unhappy are close synonyms.

clue.text: South American favourite about to be nabbed as one sought by police

parts.note: S is south
US is American

indicators.note: to be nabbed means the about letter is caught inside the favourite

parts.note: a pet is a favourite
C is circa, about

explanation.surface: A favourite South American is about to be arrested as a wanted man.
explanation.definitionFit: Police hunt a person thought guilty of a crime.

clue.text: Sound of giant to be more constrained

indicators.note: sound of signals a word that is pronounced like another

parts.note: a titan is a giant

explanation.surface: A giant's noise is restrained further.
explanation.definitionFit: To become tighter or firmer is to be more restricted.

clue.text: Sword Rear Admiral placed on support

indicators.note: placed on means in a down clue the first piece sits above the second

parts.note: a pier is a supporting pillar

explanation.surface: A naval officer's blade is set on a stand.
explanation.definitionFit: A slender, sharp-pointed blade used for thrusting is a type of sword.

clue.text: Criticising fizzy drink offered by the French doctor — no good

indicators.note: offered by places the drink after the earlier pieces that offer it

parts.note: la is French for the
MB is Bachelor of Medicine
Asti is a sparkling Italian wine
NG is no good

explanation.surface: A French doctor offers bubbly that is no good, attracting criticism.
explanation.definitionFit: Lambasting is attacking someone verbally, harshly berating them.

clue.text: Club housing old vessel

indicators.note: housing means the club word holds the old letter

parts.note: a bat is a club
O is old

explanation.surface: A club building that holds an old ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Any craft that floats on water is a vessel.

clue.text: Lines penned by queen maybe, a beautiful person

indicators.note: penned by means the lines are enclosed by the queen

parts.note: a queen bee is one example of a bee
L is line, so LL is lines

explanation.surface: A queen pens lines about a lovely person.
explanation.definitionFit: A belle is a beautiful woman, especially the most admired at a ball.

clue.text: Tiny piece of music with a final twist

indicators.note: a final twist means the last letters of the music swap places

parts.note: a minuet is a piece of dance music

explanation.surface: A little tune ending in an unexpected way.
explanation.definitionFit: Minute, pronounced my-NEWT, means extremely small.

clue.text: Get a lute to play? You need instruction

indicators.note: to play suggests the letters are played about with

explanation.surface: Buy a lute to play it and you will need lessons.
explanation.definitionFit: Tutelage is teaching, guidance from a tutor.

clue.text: Types of exams offering breaks around lunchtime?

indicators.note: around means the breaks word surrounds the lunchtime piece

parts.note: rests are breaks
lunchtime as one o'clock, i.e. the Roman numeral I

explanation.surface: Exam kinds that give pauses around lunch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'lunchtime?' is one o'clock, read as I.
explanation.definitionFit: Retakes of tests failed earlier are a kind of examination.

clue.text: Having not looked at words, not prepared, falling short

indicators.note: falling short means the word is cut short at its end

parts.note: unready means not prepared

explanation.surface: Someone who has not read the text arrives unprepared.
explanation.definitionFit: A text never perused is one nobody has looked at.
